hints: Sort coders by skill before forming groups.
Track teams that have started but whose maximum skill has not yet been chosen.
Each open team accrues the gap between consecutive skill values.
analogy: An open team accumulates one unit of penalty for every unit the scan moves past its smallest member.
example: For skills [2,3,5] and penalty limit 2, the valid partitions are all singletons, {2,3} with {5}, and {3,5} with {2}: 3.
algorithm: Sort skills. Let dp[o][c] count partial assignments with o open teams and accumulated penalty c. Before processing each coder, add o*(currentSkill-previousSkill) to c. Then place the coder in one of o open teams and leave it open, form a singleton, start a new open team, or join and close one of o open teams. These give multipliers o, 1, 1 and o respectively. Discard costs above x and work modulo 1000000007. Sum dp[0][c] for c<=x after all coders.
correctness: For every open team, each skill gap between its first and last member contributes once to its final max-minus-min penalty. The four transitions cover exactly the possible roles of the next coder, including the choice of which labeled-by-members open team to join. Only states with no open teams are complete partitions.
complexity: For n coders and penalty limit x, there are O(n^2*x) state transitions and O(n*x) rolling space.
